transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called this planning check-in so we can review the draft production plan for the spring musical together before I give my final approval. The draft currently proposes a Friday 7:00 p.m. performance with 220 audience seats, ordinary stage effects, and optional event recording. I'd like to hear from each of you -- the drama teacher, facilities manager, school nurse, and family liaison -- about any concerns or adjustments you think we need to address before I sign off on the plan.

transcript.text: I need to raise an important issue before we finalize this plan. I received an email this week from the rights holder for one of the musical numbers in our production. They confirmed that the school may perform that number only after purchasing a live-performance license, and -- critically -- they stated that any audio or video recording of the production is prohibited. I haven't yet attached this email to the activity-approval file, but I'm sharing it now so we can address it. This directly affects the draft plan's proposal for optional event recording.

transcript.text: I need to raise a critical scheduling concern. The district activity-bus coordinator confirmed that 12 participating students cannot reliably obtain evening transportation, and an activity bus is available for a Saturday 1:00 p.m. matinee. I've confirmed this with the affected families and the transportation office this week. This means the Friday 7:00 p.m. performance must be moved to the Saturday 1:00 p.m. matinee — not supplemented with an additional performance. I have not yet entered this in the event calendar, but this change is essential to ensure all cast members can participate.
